newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dow, dollar, Buba to set tone for Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Dow, dollar, Buba to set tone for Brussels bourse.

text.p: The immediate future of the Brussels bourse, which ended well in the red on Monday, lies in the hands of the gyrating U.S. stock market, the dollar and the German Bundesbank, traders said.
"There is no panic selling, but there are also no buyers," one trader said. "We are still very much under the shadow of the United States and of German interest rates."

The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares ended Monday 1.97 percent or 47.58 points lower at 2,370.29. It had fallen as much as 3.1 percent early in the session after the steep decline in New York .DJI on Friday when Belgian markets were closed.

The only one of the 20 index issues to show a closing gain a was discount retailer Colruyt, up 1.4 percent at 17,600 francs, on a weekend newspaper report saying its share of the Belgian market grew to 24 percent in the second quarter.

Traders said investors were focused on a possible increase in German interest rates this week, although the strengthening of the mark against the dollar had made the pressure for a defensive rise less intense.
"If the Germans do something on interest rates we could have a problem," one trader said. "They gave an inflation warning last week. First you warn, then you act."
"We have a problem in Europe with the dollar (strength). It is inflationary. The Germans prefer to act quite quickly. They have to maintain their image," a trader said.
Traders said charts indicated support in the Bel-20 at 2,300 points, but moves in the dollar and interest rates could either move the floor down to 2,200 or raise it.
"It is difficult to judge. It could go either way," one said. "In Brussels everything depends on the dollar."
Traders said dollar-sensitives and the less liquid stocks were among the main sufferers in the index on a day still marked by holiday absences.
Chemical and drugs firm UCB, a volatile stock at the best of times, lost 3.5 percent at 122,500 francs. Non- ferrous metals firm Union Miniere shed 1.7 percent.
Financials too fell out of favour.
Kredietbank dropped 4.6 percent. GBL fell four percent, BBL lost 1.7 percent. Generale Bank slipped 1.2 percent and holding company Societe Generale de Belgique was 3.7 percent lower.
Oil major PetroFina benefitted from a broker 'buy' recommendation to end only 0.4 percent weaker.
